newsitem.title: USA: Motorola most popular stock among investment clubs.
newsitem.headline: Motorola most popular stock among investment clubs.

text.p: Motorola Inc. is the most popular stock among America's investment clubs, replacing McDonald's Corp., which held the top stop for the past six years.

According to the National Association of Investors Corp., a not-for-profit organisation of investment clubs and individual investors, this represents "a major shift in direction for the nation's approximately 25,900 investment clubs."
Five high-technology companies were among the top 20 popular stocks of the year, according to the list published in the April edition of Better Investing magazine.
In addition to Motorola, other high-technology stocks in the top 10 were Intel Corp. (No. 5); Lucent Technologies (No. 8); RPM Inc. (No. 9); and AT&T Corp. (No.10).
McDonald's dropped to fourth place in the 1997 rankings. Rounding out the top 10 were PepsiCo Inc. (No. 2); Merck & Co. Inc. (No.3); and AFLAC Inc. (No. 6).
Wal-Mart Stores Inc., No. 8 in 1996, dropped to No. 20 this year.

"Our counsel to members has always been to invest in growth companies that are positioned to grow in value in five years, and club members are now identifying more high-technology firms for long-term investment," said NAIC President Kenneth Janke.
In 1997, about a dozen high-technology or computer-related firms made it into the top 100.
